_meta.why: The seasonality engine (§9.3) needs labelled expectations for Indian calendar events even in year 1, before it has 2+ years of the user's own data to learn from. Without priors, festival and tax-season spending surprises the forecast.
_meta.what: Indian calendar events with the categories they inflate and a prior multiplier, plus the shrinkage rule that blends these priors with the user's observed history.
_meta.result: 'October festival spending typically +38% for you - plan INR 6,500 extra' style insights and inputs to the cash-flow forecast and budget suggestions.
changelog: 2026-07-17 — Created from SRS v1.7 §9.3. Priors are starter multipliers, superseded by the user's own seasonal index as data accrues.

2026-09-19 — 1.1 (issue 9.3): added the `method` block, SEAS-INDEX, so the shrinkage denominator, the history window and the minimum effect the seasonality engine reads are data with an id and a version, not prose. No event changed.
_meta.shrinkage_rule: seasonal_index = 1 + k*(raw-1), k = months_observed/24. Priors below are the 'raw' expectation used until the user's own median-based index dominates.
_meta.note: Dates are approximate windows (many festivals follow the lunar calendar); the app resolves exact dates from the /v1/knowledge/calendar feed per year.

method.why: §9.3's index needs numbers the prose rule above leaves implicit: the shrinkage denominator (k = months_observed/24), how many closed months of history the per-category median reads, and how large an effect on a month's everyday spend must be before it counts at all — smaller effects are noise, neither applied to the forecast nor named to the user. As a row they are cited in evidence (AI-ARC-006) and edited here, not in an engine.
